To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genes encoding the L4 ribosome proteins from the hyper-thermophilic Thermotoga marittima and halophilic Haloarcula mari-smorui bacteria were cloned under the control and overexpressed in Escherichia colii.

we have cloned the genes for the hyperthermophile T. maritma and the halophile H. marismartui L4 ribosomal protein, and have developed efficient purification procedures and crystallization protocols that yielded crystals suitable for structure determination.

the genes for the L. marismortiui and Thermotoga marimortui L4 ribosomal protein have been cloned under the control o a T7 promoter and expressed in E. coli, that efficient purification procedures were established to yield material suitable or crystallization trials, and that crystals were obtained of the T. marimortiui L4 protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional analysis of the bacterial and archaeal ribosomal L4 proteins.

the structure determination and functional analysis of ribosomal proteins from extremophilic organisms, which are of particular interest because of their unusual amino acid compositions and their high thermostability.
the structural analysis of proteins involved in the ribosomal peptidyl transferase reaction and in the regulation of ribosome synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the L4 proteins from the hyper-thermophilic bacteria and the halophilc archaeon can be crystallized and that the crystals diffract to a sufficient resolution to allow the structures to be solved by the molecular replacement technique.
the halophilic nature of the protein does not affect the crystallization and structure determination process.
the halophiles are not that different from other microorganisms, and that the same procedures can be applied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for the L4 proteins, we have established a successful protocol for the expression and purification of halophilic archaeal proteins and that the L4 proteins are good candidates for structure determination.
the halophilic L4 proteins crystallize under similar conditions to those of the mesophilic L4 protein.
the L4 ribosome proteins from both T. maritma and H. marismotui are crystallizable and that the crystals diffract to high resolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the L4 ribosome protein is amenable to crystallization and that the crystals obtained are of sufficient quality to be suitable for X-ray structure determination.
the L4 proteins from both organisms are amenable to crystallization, and that the crystals of T. marittima L4 are sufficiently well ordered to allow structure determination by molecular replacement.
halophilic archaeal proteins can be successfully expressed and purified in E. coli.
